column1: # One row per rule of this increment that a gate-runnable Go test discharges, in the three id spaces the
#   D1–D4   the goal's four `Done when` clauses, in order
#   B1–B3   the goal's three `Bounds` clauses, in order;
#   O1–O12  the rules of AGENTS.md §"OpenCode is a target whose store only the harness writes", in the
#   R1–R12  the rules of AGENTS.md's dialogue boundary — the semantic rule ("A record's dialogue is the
#           source's own answer or the record's own bytes, never a reading of them") and the disclosed-outcome
#           rule that follows it ("Where the read answered no projection, the outcome is disclosed, never
#           guessed") — plus the OpenCode paragraph's tool-part instant and record-instant rules, in the
# scripts/obligation-citations.py is the arbiter: every row's cited test must exist in the named package
# and run and pass, and the `citations` step is required — a tree that lost this file, or a citation that
# went stale, fails the gate instead of passing partially. Columns: rule_id, test, package, artifact.
# Tab-separated; `#` comments and blank lines are ignored; a rule id appears once.
# Deliberately not covered, with the reason (form-based: a row is one Go test in a package
# scripts/gate-targets.txt covers, so a rule whose gate evidence is a python case the required `selftest`
# step runs, or a native harness run, cannot hold one):
#   O12 — the native check's planting and removal discipline (the id read before planting, only the
#            check's own leftover removed through the harness's own `session delete`, a failed planting
#            reconciled as the route reconciles one). Its evidence is the native run
#            scripts/tests/test_opencode_native_check.py the `selftest` step runs — a native harness run
#            and a python case, not a Go test.
# Two evidence halves belong to clauses whose rows hold their Go-test half; they are named here rather
# than dropped: D1's native load/export/resume arm is that same native run, and D4's "source-side
# AgentsView parity remains intact" is the gate's required `parity` step (scripts/upstream-parity.py),
# while its "existing Claude-to-Codex route remains intact" half is a property of the accepted routes'
# existing suites the gate's `test` step runs, not any single Go test.
